works.title: Roman Cavalry Face Helmet from Nijmegen

orientation.note: Source-reference and ten-view visual review, 2026-10-07. Selected variant B; complete surviving object and authored appearance retained.

works.geometryReview: Reviewed the exact immutable derivative against the Erfgoed Gelderland / Valkhof Museum source thumbnail and all ten candidate orientations. It retains the complete surviving Roman face helmet: face mask with ears, hinged decorated forehead band and its small busts, extant helmet material and neck guard. The missing upper helmet bowl is the source-documented archaeological loss, not a defect to reconstruct. Variant B, +Y/[0,0,0]/yaw0, places the forehead above the eyes, nose and chin, with the exterior face toward the initial camera. The curved metallic element below/behind the face belongs to the surviving helmet/neck-guard scope; no modern mount enters the measured Y bound. Museum height 24.2 cm is the documented complete-surviving-object measurement, including its extant neck guard. Height binding would give whole X width 25.05 cm, versus the museum width 22.8 cm; this is one documented height-axis calibration and must not be described as complete two-axis agreement. Final scale decision: exact/verified AR stays disabled pending proportion reconciliation. Height calibration Y=0.242 m would imply width 0.250548 m instead of the source 0.228 m, about 9.9% larger; decoded mesh-local extents are a unit cube and preserved source-world proportions do not reconcile this discrepancy.

works.title: Montefortino Helmet from Piquete de la Atalaya

orientation.note: Source-reference and ten-view visual review, 2026-10-07. Selected variant B; complete surviving object and authored appearance retained.

works.geometryReview: Reviewed the exact immutable derivative against the Museo de Zaragoza source thumbnail and all ten candidate orientations. It retains the surviving Montefortino helmet bowl, crown knob, lower rim, original neck projection and surviving attachment details, with the source-authored copper-alloy/corrosion appearance. Variant B, +Y/[0,0,0]/yaw0, gives the upright exterior front with crown knob above and helmet opening down; interior and rear views confirm that there is no separate museum support or reconstructed cheek piece in the mesh. The documented height 20.8 cm would supply a conditional whole-object Y direction if measurement and derivative proportions reconcile. Whole precise source-world XYZ bounds are 0.184613 / 0.231052 / 0.231462 source units; assigning Y=0.208 m gives X=0.166194 m and Z=0.208369 m. These do not reproduce the source width 18 cm/depth 26.5 cm, so do not claim exact agreement of all three axes. Final scale decision: exact/verified AR stays disabled pending proportion reconciliation. Height calibration Y=0.208 m would imply width 0.166194 m and depth 0.208369 m instead of source 0.18 / 0.265 m, about 7.7% / 21.4% smaller. The preserved whole bounds do not reconcile these proportions.

works.title: Roman Cavalry Harness Pendant from Maastricht

orientation.note: Source-reference and ten-view visual review, 2026-10-07. Supplemental rendered source-front pose confirmed; readable inventory writing at upper-right, loop up and pendant lobe down.

works.geometryReview: Reviewed the exact immutable derivative against the Centre Ceramique Maastricht source thumbnail, the complete ten-view sheet and a supplementary rendered source-front candidate. It retains the suspension loop, two broad side lobes, lower central hanging lobe, irregular archaeological edges, brass/corrosion surface and readable museum inventory writing. The material is double-sided and unlit. Sheet J is upright but exposes the reverse of the scanned face, making inventory writing reversed and swapping the source left/right surface features. Applying a world-Y 180-degree turn to J is exactly equivalent to +Y/modelRotation [90,90,0]/yaw0. The actual supplementary thumbnail confirms this final pose: loop above, hanging lobe below, green corrosion at left and readable inventory writing at upper-right, matching the author source image. No modern support is present. The source explicitly gives approximate 7 × 7 cm only; no exact calibration or verified-size AR eligibility is justified.
